newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: "Mr Clean" named S.Korean ruling party chairman.
newsitem.headline: "Mr Clean" named S.Korean ruling party chairman.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam has named a former judge, dubbed "Mr Clean", as new chairman of his ruling party as part of a power play ahead of presidential polls this year.
The nomination of Lee Hoi-chang will be confirmed at a caucus of the New Korea Party on Thursday, a presidential Blue House official said.
Lee is best known for quitting as Kim's prime minister in 1994 in protest at curbs on his power.
By standing up to the president, he strengthened his reputation for independence and for refusing to compromise his principles.
Lee is one of nine party leaders -- known as the "nine dragons" -- tipped as contenders for the party's nomination as presidential candidate in elections in December.
Kim is barred by the constitution from seeking a second term, but political analysts say he will try to work behind the scenes to put in place a successor.
Some analysts speculated that Kim, in naming Lee party chairman, was indicating his preference for him as president.

Lee added to his reputation for integrity by urging the government to reopen an investigation into a bribes-for-loans scandal involving Hanbo Steel Co, which collapsed under a mountain of debt in January.
Opposition parties have called the probe a whitewash and are particularly incensed that it exonerated Kim's second son Kim Hyun-chul.
The scandal has landed three of Kim's closest associates behind bars on bribery charges and further tarnished his image as a graft-buster.
There was a fresh twist on Tuesday in the race for the presidency when another of the "nine dragons" suffered an apparent stroke.
Choi Hyung-woo, 61, headed a faction of Kim loyalists within the ruling New Korea Party.

Last month, Kim dumped four top presidential Blue House aides as part of a sweeping administration reshuffle designed to restore his credibility after the Hanbo scandal. He also changed his prime minister and reshuffled his cabinet.
Outgoing party chairman, Lee Hong-koo, kicked off the race for the presidency on Tuesday by become the first person to declare an intention to run.
